title: Nonvanishing of top local cohomology of a Noetherian local ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak n)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], meaning that $\mathfrak n$ is its unique maximal ideal, with finite Krull dimension $d=\dim\operatorname{Spec}R\geq0$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For an $R$-module $M$, put $\Gamma_{\mathfrak n}(M)=\{x\in M:\mathfrak n^nx=0\text{ for some }n\geq1\}$ and $H^j_{\mathfrak n}(M)=R^j\Gamma_{\mathfrak n}(M)$. Then $H^d_{\mathfrak n}(R)\ne0$.

proof.text: Put $A=\widehat R=\varprojlim_nR/\mathfrak n^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] it is Noetherian, and by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] it is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak nA$ and residue field $R/\mathfrak n$; in particular it is nonzero. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension], $\dim A=d$. The canonical map $R\to A$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] with $M=R$ and $I=\mathfrak n$, $A$ is complete as an $R$-module for the $\mathfrak n$-adic filtration. For each $k$, $(\mathfrak nA)^k=\mathfrak n^kA$: both ideals consist of sums of products of $k$ elements from the image of $\mathfrak n$, with coefficients in $A$. Thus the quotients defining that module completion are exactly $A/\mathfrak m^k$, and $A\to\varprojlim_kA/\mathfrak m^k$ is a ring isomorphism. Hence $A$ is a complete Noetherian local ring.

source.place: Tag 0DXE (lemma-cd-maximal), completion paragraph; algebra.tex Tags 0316, 05GG, 00MC and more-algebra.tex Tag 07NV.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-power-series-presentation] to the complete local ring $A$. It supplies a surjective local homomorphism $q:S\to A$ from a complete Noetherian regular local ring $S$. By [lem-trf-regular-local-bounded-injective-resolution], $S[0]$ has a bounded injective representative $J$. Its only cohomology is the finite cyclic module $S$ in degree zero. To check its scalar-action map, $J$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], so [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] computes $R\operatorname{Hom}_S(S[0],S[0])$ by $\operatorname{Hom}_S(S[0],J)$. Evaluation at $1$ identifies this complex with $J$, including differentials, and the scalar-action map becomes the chosen quasi-isomorphism $S[0]\to J$. Thus the scalar-action map is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0BFR (lemma-ubiquity-dualizing), proof of case (2): Cohen presentation and the regular local ring.

proof.text: The quotient $A$ is a finite $S$-module, generated by $1$. The rings $S,A$ are Noetherian, and Step 2 verified every condition on $L=S[0]$ in [lem-trf-finite-map-dualizing-transfer]. Apply that statement: $\Omega=R\operatorname{Hom}_S(A,S[0])$ has finite $A$-cohomology, a bounded injective $A$-representative, and the scalar-action isomorphism over $A$. These are exactly the three conditions for an algebraic dualizing complex in [def-per-algebraic-normalized-dualizing]. By [lem-per-algebraic-local-dualizing-normalization] there is an integer $s$ such that $\omega=\Omega[-s]$ is normalized. In particular every $H^j(\omega)$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 0BFR (lemma-ubiquity-dualizing), case (2), with Tags 0AX0, 0A7L and the normalization in 0A7M.

proof.text: Use the prime-chain definition of dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], which also identifies it with the topological dimension used in the item. Since $\dim A=d$ is finite and $A\ne0$, a chain $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_d$ exists: a supremum of nonnegative integer lengths equal to $d$ is attained. Its first prime $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_0$ is minimal, since a smaller prime could be prepended to give length $d+1$. Primes of $A/\mathfrak p$ correspond by inverse image to primes of $A$ containing $\mathfrak p$, preserving strict inclusion: the inverse sends $\mathfrak q$ to $\mathfrak q/\mathfrak p$ and primality follows directly by multiplying representatives. The displayed chain therefore gives dimension at least $d$ in the quotient, and every chain in the quotient lifts to one in $A$, giving dimension at most $d$. Thus $\dim(A/\mathfrak p)=d$. This also covers $d=0$.

source.place: Tag 0A7V (lemma-nonvanishing-generically-local), choosing a top-dimensional minimal prime for its application in Tag 0DXE.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-algebraic-dualizing-generic-degree] to $(A,\mathfrak m)$, $\omega$, and the minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of Step 4 with $e=d$. Its hypotheses hold by Steps 1, 3 and 4. It gives $H^{-d}(\omega)_{\mathfrak p}\ne0$. Consequently $N=H^{-d}(\omega)\ne0$, since the localization of the zero module is zero. The module $N$ is finitely generated by Step 3.

source.place: Tag 0A7V (lemma-nonvanishing-generically-local), the last nonvanishing cited in Tag 0DXE.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-algebraic-local-duality] to $A$, $\omega$, $M=A$ and $i=d$. It supplies an injective hull $E$ of the residue field and an isomorphism $\widehat{\operatorname{Ext}^{-d}_A(A,\omega)}\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(H^d_{\mathfrak m}(A),E)$. The first Ext module equals $H^{-d}(\omega)=N$: using [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], evaluation at $1$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_A(A[0],I)$ with $I$ for a K-injective representative $I$ of $\omega$, hence $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A[0],\omega)\cong\omega$. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor], $\widehat N\cong\widehat A\otimes_A N$, since $A$ is Noetherian and $N$ is finite. Step 1 established that $A\to\widehat A$ is an isomorphism, so this tensor product is isomorphic to $A\otimes_A N\cong N$, with $a\otimes x\mapsto ax$ and inverse $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. Therefore $\widehat N\ne0$, and the local-duality isomorphism forces $H^d_{\mathfrak m}(A)\ne0$: otherwise its Hom module would be zero.

source.place: Tag 0AAK (lemma-special-case-local-duality), K=A[0]; algebra.tex Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), for the completion of the finite module N.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-local-cohomology-flat-base-change] to $R\to A$, $I=\mathfrak n$, $M=R$ and $q=d$. Both rings are Noetherian and the map is flat by Step 1; the extended ideal is $\mathfrak m$. Since $R\otimes_R A\cong A$, it gives $H^d_{\mathfrak n}(R)\otimes_R A\cong H^d_{\mathfrak m}(A)$. The right side is nonzero by Step 6. If $H^d_{\mathfrak n}(R)$ were zero, its tensor product would be zero, a contradiction. This proves the stated nonvanishing over the original ring $R$.
